description: Fades in the start and fades out the end of a soundfile ('dovetailing') without needing an envelope breakpoint file. Pinned to submode 1 (chosen fade shapes per end); submode 2 (fixed doubly-exponential slopes) is reproducible from this entry with intype/outtype 3 - verified byte-identical - so it need not be curated separately. Duration model static and exact (fades reshape amplitude in place; verified edge RMS dropped to 1-3% of the source while the middle is untouched). Works on mono and stereo input.
musical_use: The bread-and-butter fade utility: smooth a click at either edge of an edited file, or let a sound emerge slowly out of silence and return to it (the fade durations can be arbitrarily long, up to the point where the two would overlap). Linear slopes (0) give a steady rise/fall; exponential (1, the documented default) is slower then faster on the way up, faster then slower on the way down - usually the more natural choice. The undocumented steeper shapes (2 'steep', 3 'doubly exponential') push the knee harder toward the file body. CDP's own filter documentation recommends dovetailing long silent-ish tails before filtering, which otherwise computes drastically slower.

infadedur.description: Duration of the fade-in at the start of the file (seconds by default; samples or grouped-samples if the times flag is set). infadedur + outfadedur must not exceed the input duration - the binary aborts with 'ERROR: Start and End Trims overlap: cannot proceed.'. Negative values die with an unhelpful 'INSUFFICIENT MEMORY to reallocate level array.' rather than a range message. Scalar only.

outfadedur.description: Duration of the fade-out at the end of the file (same units and overlap constraint as infadedur). Scalar only.

intype.description: Envelope shape of the fade-in: 0 = linear, 1 = exponential (the documented default, emitted when unset). The binary also accepts undocumented 2 = 'steep' and 3 = 'doubly exponential' (source-confirmed ENVTYPE enum; 3 reproduces envel dovetail mode 2 exactly). 4+ or negative values abort with internal errors, not range messages. Scalar only.

outtype.description: Envelope shape of the fade-out; same values and caveats as intype. Scalar only.

times.description: Unit of the fade durations: 0 = seconds (the default when the flag is omitted), 1 = samples, 2 = grouped-samples (one stereo frame counts as 1). Out-of-range values abort with the internal error 'Unknown case: ENV_DOVETAILING: envelope_preprocess()' rather than a range message. Scalar only.

examples.expected_use: Remove clicks/abruptness at both ends; duration unchanged.

examples.description: Slow emergence and disappearance, linear slopes.
examples.expected_use: Sound rises steadily out of silence and sinks back; fades may be any length that does not overlap.

known_issues: UNDOCUMENTED VALUES: intype/outtype accept 0-3, not the documented 0-1. Source (dev/include/envlcon.h + env/envfuncs.c) defines ENVTYPE_LIN=0, EXP=1, STEEP=2, DBL=3; probes confirm 2 and 3 produce distinct outputs and 'dovetail 1 ... 3 3' is byte-identical to 'dovetail 2' with the same fade durations. Values outside 0-3 are not range-checked: they abort with 'ERROR: Unknown case in create_envelope()' or 'ERROR: INTERNAL ERROR: (Bug?)'.
Fade overlap is runtime-enforced against the input duration: infadedur 1.2 + outfadedur 1.2 on a 2 s file aborts with 'ERROR: Start and End Trims overlap: cannot proceed.'
A negative infadedur is not range-checked; it aborts with the misleading 'ERROR: INSUFFICIENT MEMORY to reallocate level array.'
All five parameters reject breakpoint files ('ERROR: Cannot read parameter N [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.', N = 1-5); for envelope shapes beyond two fades use envel create/envel impose instead.
